t: You're at Battersea Bridge, a five-span arch bridge with cast-iron girders and granite piers, linking Battersea on the south bank with Chelsea on the north. It sits on a sharp bend in the Thames, and it replaced a ferry that had run near here since at least the middle of the sixteenth century. The engineer Joseph Bazalgette designed it. He's best remembered for London's main drainage system, built after the Great Stink of 1858, which helped free the city from cholera and began cleaning the river.
